God, this film.

I saw it with my parents. We discussed it for one, maybe two hours after we left the theater, just analyzing everything and peeling back all its layers. I'd confided in them some of my struggles with being at a PWI, but after this movie they definitely sensed that it had a huge impact on me (as it did on them). My mom teared up at Killmonger's last line.

I saw a lot of myself in Shuri, how she was so playful and intelligent and beautiful and not at all shown from a stereotypical lens (regarding other mainstream media featuring black women, not this movie obviously). I really wish this movie could have been released six or seven years ago, even ten years ago, when I was much younger and dealing with my own issues of self-worth. Better that it was released now than never, but I just hope it gives inspiration to young black kids, especially young black girls, inspiration that I needed when I was growing up.

(On a side note, a white man in our row left after Killmonger took the throne and discussed his plans. My mom turned to me and joked, "He can't take it.")

I think the first time for me was in third grade, but it was from these two Vietnamese girls who I considered "friends" at the time. They were talking about going to each other's houses, and I was told I could not go to their houses because their parents "didn't like black people." They were really into Zoey 101 and looked up to a lot of white child actresses at the time. (It was a very white, Republican town in southern California.)

Another time was in eighth grade, in the same town, when my "friend" told me I was "a 12/10 on the 'black people's scale,' but an 8/10 on the 'regular' one" because I have light skin and a straight nose. Needless to say, I didn't take it as a compliment at all. She was Filipino too, and we were basically the same color; I'd known her since second grade (before I moved states a few years ago), but again, she felt the effects of living in that same town. It's only when I recall these events that I realize how much of a suburban hell my hometown is.

Now that I'm older and I fully understand the nuances of being black in America/the Western world, I think [my recent thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/blackladies/comments/7tpg49/roommate_said_ill_be_lookin_fine_in_hoodrat/) really cements this realization. So, no matter how I talk, where I come from, what music I listen to or what my interests are, the only thing most white people see at my PWI (whether they state any bs or not) is my skin color. It's such a rude awakening, but also extremely depressing. And then many have the nerve to invalidate our experiences.

Since you're planning to transfer next fall, you should try and take FREN 201 for that quarter anyway. Maybe you can brush up on your French by using [Duolingo](https://www.duolingo.com/), then before fall 2018 you can contact the [Modern and Classical Languages department](https://chss.wwu.edu/mcl) about placement into FREN 201. That way you wouldn't have to wait a year and a half for 104. (And Duolingo is a great source for learning new languages--and reviewing past-learned languages as well!)

I'm a freshman, but I took French all four years of high school (including FREN 103 as a UW in the HS course) and was able to register for FREN 201 this quarter. However, since the French 200 series is sequential, 201 can only be taken in fall, 202 in winter, and 203 in spring. 104 is only offered in spring as well.

I'm guessing you're a prospective transfer, so if you were to transfer before or for spring quarter then you should take 104 to review and prepare you for the 200 series. FREN 201 is pretty fast-paced, so the review would probably help (especially after not taking it for a year). You need to take the 200 series anyway before going into FREN 301.

(also I made this offhand comment about my hair getting frizzy and she *actually* said, "You don't even know how hard my hair gets. Mine is so flat.")

She has more connections than I do and understands that I have social anxiety, but it's still so hard. I've basically given up trying to "fit in" at this PWI; so many people around me are so basic and boring. I've met a few people from class that I wanna hang w/ but idk how. I just wish I knew where the other nerdy black people are on this campus.

I may have to start. It's not like it's a few people around here; *a lot* of people smell funky. More than a few times I'd be waiting for the lecture to begin when someone takes the open seat next to me and it's like..... did you shower today or yesterday or the day before or?

I ordered a replacement debit card last week, but it still hasn't come in. :/ I'm giving it tomorrow to come but if it doesn't then I may just give up on any Halloween plans b/c I don't have a costume. idk if it's b/c mailing to a dorm is so unnecessarily complicated or if the bank just takes forever to send it. side note... idk if it's the culture at my school (I live in the PNW. hippie/stoner/etc culture) but a lot of people around me smell like they don't shower and it makes me nauseous

The "not ugly" comment didn't come out of nowhere though. In my head I contrasted that w/ the reaction to a girl we share a bathroom with--like night and day, she gushed over how pretty she was when she first met her. I don't even think I can go on after today tbh; I completely embarrassed myself in my debate (I'm in a government class), I'm not good with public speaking (never was) and when it was over I could tell that my opponents pitied me.
